name: Self-exciting point processes for crime and conflict: Mohler et al. 2011 (crime/ETAS), Lewis et al. 2012 (Iraq civilian deaths), Zammit-Mangion et al. 2012 (Afghan War Diary), Cseke et al. 2016 (sparse inference for spatio-temporal LGCP), Bahid et al. 2024 (Euromaidan Hawkes)
url: Mohler 2011: https://doi.org/10.1198/jasa.2011.ap09546 ; Lewis 2012: https://www.math.ucla.edu/~bertozzi/papers/iraq.pdf (CAM report https://ww3.math.ucla.edu/camreport/cam10-38.pdf) ; Zammit-Mangion 2012: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3411944 ; Cseke 2016: https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.4152 (JASA DOI 10.1080/01621459.2015.1115357) ; Bahid 2024: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.12253 (PLOS ONE 19(5): e0301639)
authors: Mohler, Short, Brantingham, Schoenberg, Tita (2011); Lewis, Mohler, Brantingham, Bertozzi (2012); Zammit-Mangion, Dewar, Kadirkamanathan, Sanguinetti (2012); Cseke, Zammit-Mangion, Heskes, Sanguinetti (2016); Bahid, Kutsenko, Rodriguez, White (2024)
popularity: Mohler 2011 is the seminal crime-Hawkes paper (well over 1,000 citations) and the basis of PredPol; Lewis 2012 and Zammit-Mangion 2012 are widely cited in conflict modelling (low hundreds); Cseke 2016 is a methods paper (tens of citations); Bahid 2024 is recent with few citations. Exact counts not retrieved [uncertain]
peer_review_status: peer-reviewed (JASA, Security Journal, PNAS, JASA, PLOS ONE)
target_type: Event intensity (count/rate of new events), i.e. an ONSET-type target by construction: a Hawkes/ETAS model predicts the conditional rate of new event arrivals lambda(t, s | history). There is no 'state' (ongoing) label, so state-target inflation does not arise. Cseke/Zammit-Mangion model a latent log-Gaussian Cox intensity (counts per cell per time step), not explicit self-excitation, but still a count/onset target.
target_definition: Mohler 2011: lambda(t,x,y) = mu(x,y) + sum over past events of g(t - t_i, x - x_i, y - y_i) (ETAS-style branching); forecasts are next-day intensity per 150 m grid cell, ranked to flag hotspots. Lewis 2012: temporal Hawkes lambda(t) = mu(t) + sum k*omega*exp(-omega*(t-t_i)) on daily civilian-death event counts per district, with three variants for a time-varying background mu(t). Zammit-Mangion 2012: discrete-time spatio-temporal LGCP, monthly/yearly event counts on a spatial basis over Afghanistan; forward prediction of 2010 counts from 2004-2009. Cseke 2016: same LGCP class, sparse discretised state, intensity reconstruction. Bahid 2024: multivariate Hawkes over Ukrainian oblasts for daily protest events, 2013. None uses a 1-hour binary onset label; horizons range from one day to one year.
spatial_unit: Mohler: grid cells (~150 m) in Los Angeles (San Fernando Valley burglary). Lewis: four Iraqi districts (Karkh, Mosul, Fallujah, Najaf), modelled separately. Zammit-Mangion/Cseke: continuous space on a basis/grid over Afghanistan (province-level summaries). Bahid: Ukrainian oblasts incl. Kyiv (multivariate, cross-oblast excitation).
at_risk_masking: Not applicable in the same sense: point-process likelihoods are defined over the full timeline and count arrivals, not states. There is no 'already under event' state because events are instantaneous. For alerts (events with duration) a Hawkes onset model would need an explicit choice: either treat onsets as points and ignore duration (intensity can be positive while an alert is active), or censor intensity during active alerts, which is the analogue of our at-risk mask. None of these papers addresses this.
data_sources: Mohler 2011: LAPD residential burglaries, San Fernando Valley, ~2004-2005 [uncertain on exact period]. Lewis 2012: Iraq Body Count civilian-death incidents, 2003-2007. Zammit-Mangion 2012 and Cseke 2016: WikiLeaks Afghan War Diary (tens of thousands of military-logged events), 2004-2009, with 2010 held out in Zammit-Mangion. Bahid 2024: protest event data from the Center for Social and Labor Research (Ukraine), 2013 (pre-Euromaidan and first part of Euromaidan).
data_source_variant: Not applicable (no Ukrainian air-raid alert data). All datasets are event logs with reporting biases (police reports, media-based IBC counts, military logs, protest monitors). Bahid 2024 is the only Ukrainian, oblast-level example, but the events are protests, not alerts.
preprocessing: Mohler: geocoded points; repeat/near-repeat events retained (they are the signal). Lewis: aggregation of incidents to daily time stamps per district; handling of ties is a practical issue in daily data. Zammit-Mangion/Cseke: spatial discretisation onto basis functions, annual/monthly binning. Bahid: threshold applied to daily protest spikes to make self-excitation identifiable; the authors acknowledge data inconsistencies. No deduplication or standing-event logic is described in any of them [uncertain on fine details].
known_label_artefacts: Generic issues these papers flag that transfer to alerts: (1) tied timestamps from coarse time binning (daily data) distort Hawkes kernel estimation; our alerts have minute timestamps but 113,845 exact duplicate rows must be removed first, otherwise duplicates look like extreme self-excitation (CLAUDE.md data rule: deduplicate first). (2) Reporting/collection artefacts (IBC media coverage, military logging intensity) are confounded with true intensity; analogous to the 2025 raion/hromada reform, which multiplies alert rows per oblast and would inflate a naive Hawkes branching ratio unless intervals are unioned per oblast first. (3) Non-stationary background: Lewis shows a constant mu wrongly attributes trend to self-excitation; analogous to the Jan-2025 drone surge and the Sep-2026 yellow/red reform. (4) Bahid needed a spike threshold to fit, i.e. results are sensitive to event-definition choices. None of the papers deals with event durations, so standing alerts (D-020) and the Aug-30 to Sep-1 recording gap have no direct analogue; a gap must be handled as an unobserved window in the likelihood, not as zero events.
model_family: Hawkes / ETAS self-exciting point processes (Mohler 2011 non-parametric stochastic-declustering EM with kernel density estimates of background and triggering; Lewis 2012 parametric exponential-kernel Hawkes with time-varying background; Bahid 2024 multivariate Hawkes with oblast interaction matrices based on distance vs political/voting affinity). Spatio-temporal log-Gaussian Cox processes with integro-difference dynamics (Zammit-Mangion 2012; Cseke 2016 adds sparse expectation-propagation / message passing plus structured variational Bayes for parameters).
features: Point-process models have no feature table; the analogues are: (a) background rate mu - Mohler spatial KDE, Lewis constant / piecewise / smoothed time-varying mu, Bahid per-oblast mu; maps to climatology + recent-rate baselines; (b) self-excitation kernel g(t - t_i) - exponential decay in time (Lewis: excitation lasts at most 2-6 weeks; Mohler: near-repeat on the scale of days and ~100s of metres); maps to minutes_since_last_start and exponentially-weighted onset counts; (c) cross-excitation between units - Bahid's oblast-to-oblast matrix (political affinity beat geographic distance; Kyiv activity drove nationwide dynamics); maps to neighbors_active_at_t and national_active_count_at_t; (d) external covariates - Bahid adds government use of force and injury counts as exogenous excitation; Zammit-Mangion uses spatial diffusion/relocation dynamics. No calendar features in these papers.
external_feature_timing: Bahid 2024 uses observed (same-period) government-force and injury counts as covariates in an in-sample fit; these are not forecast-time-safe in a real-time setting and would be oracle features if used for prediction. The other papers use only past events (fully causal by construction of the Hawkes conditional intensity). For our project: any Hawkes-style feature is causal only if computed from onsets with start time <= t.
ablation_design: Bahid 2024 compares six nested Hawkes variants (adding self-excitation, external influence, regional effects, injuries) on the same data by negative log-likelihood and AIC; regional (oblast) effects gave the main improvement. Lewis 2012 compares three background-rate variants on the same districts/period. These are same-sample comparisons but mostly IN-SAMPLE (likelihood/AIC), not out-of-sample forecast skill [uncertain for Lewis].
split_scheme: Mohler 2011: rolling one-day-ahead forecasts, model fit on past data, evaluated on the next day's burglaries (prospective, walk-forward style). Zammit-Mangion 2012: fit 2004-2009, forecast 2010 (single chronological hold-out). Lewis 2012: primarily in-sample model comparison over 2003-2007 [uncertain]. Cseke 2016: methodological, reconstruction/in-sample plus simulations. Bahid 2024: in-sample fit on 2013 data (NLL/AIC).
metrics: Mohler 2011: fraction of next-day crimes captured in the top-k% of flagged cells (hit-rate vs area curve), compared with prospective hotspot maps. Lewis 2012: log-likelihood/AIC and estimated branching ratio. Zammit-Mangion 2012: posterior predictive coverage of 2010 counts (claims 'strikingly statistically accurate' forward prediction). Cseke 2016: approximation accuracy vs MCMC, runtime. Bahid 2024: NLL and AIC. None reports Brier, BSS, ROC-AUC or PR-AUC.
unit_of_metric: Mohler: pooled over the city grid; Lewis: per district; Zammit-Mangion: pooled/aggregated spatial counts; Bahid: pooled likelihood over all oblasts.
baseline_strength: Mohler 2011 beats a prospective hotspot (recency-weighted KDE) baseline, which is a strong recent-rate-type baseline; reported gains are modest in absolute crime capture. Lewis 2012 explicitly shows that a constant background is a weak baseline and that self-excitation share drops when background is allowed to vary - i.e. part of 'self-excitation' is really a slowly changing recent rate. Zammit-Mangion and Bahid do not compare against a rolling recent-rate or climatology forecaster. None uses calibrated persistence.
calibration: Not reported as reliability plots. Zammit-Mangion gives posterior predictive intervals (a form of distributional calibration on counts). Hawkes models can be checked with time-rescaling residuals / compensator QQ plots, which is the point-process analogue of a reliability check; usage in these papers is not confirmed [uncertain].
calibration_under_drift: Lewis 2012 is the most relevant: it shows the background rate in Iraq is non-stationary (surge periods) and that ignoring this inflates the estimated self-excitation fraction. No paper tests calibration-in-the-large on a later regime. Bahid finds self-excitation already present before Euromaidan and intensifying during it - a parameter shift across regimes, which implies a fitted kernel would need refitting after a regime change.
uncertainty_of_gain: No block bootstrap or Diebold-Mariano test on forecast-skill differences. Bayesian papers give posterior uncertainty on parameters/intensity; Lewis/Bahid give likelihood-based comparisons only.
regime_coverage: Not applicable to UA alert regimes. Within their domains: Lewis spans the 2006-2007 Iraq surge (non-stationary background); Zammit-Mangion forecasts 2010 (escalation year) from 2004-2009; Bahid spans pre-protest to protest onset in 2013.
leakage_handling: Hawkes conditional intensity is causal by construction (depends only on events before t), so feature leakage is structurally hard. Remaining risks visible in these papers: (1) parameters (mu, kernel, branching ratio) fitted on the full period and then used to 'explain' the same period - in-sample (Lewis, Bahid, Cseke); (2) non-parametric background KDEs (Mohler) must be fitted only on the past for each forecast day - Mohler does a prospective fit; (3) Bahid's exogenous covariates are contemporaneous. For our project the analogues are D-021 (fit on train only, freeze), the purge rule at cut-offs, and the truncation leakage test: an exponentially-decayed onset count must give identical values when the data are truncated at t.
test_window_hygiene: No pre-registration in any paper. Zammit-Mangion 2012 has a clean one-shot forward test (2010 held out). Mohler uses a rolling prospective evaluation. Lewis and Bahid are explanatory model comparisons without a held-out test.
headline_results: Mohler 2011: ETAS/Hawkes forecasting captured more next-day burglaries in the top flagged cells than prospective hotspot maps (paper reports improvement in crime-capture at fixed area; exact numbers not retrieved [uncertain]); later field trials (Mohler et al. 2015 JASA) reported 1.4-2.2x more crimes predicted than analysts. Lewis 2012: self-excitation accounts for up to 37-50% of violent events in Iraqi districts, with excitation lasting at most 2-6 weeks depending on district; branching processes judged well suited but background non-stationarity matters. Zammit-Mangion 2012: accurate forward prediction of 2010 armed-opposition activity from prior years, with uncertainty, and identification of diffusion/relocation/escalation patterns. Cseke 2016: scalable sparse approximate inference with moderate accuracy loss vs exact methods, applied to reconstruct Afghan conflict intensity. Bahid 2024: self-excitation pre-existed and intensified during Euromaidan; oblast-specific effects gave the main NLL/AIC improvement; government force correlated with more future protests; political affinity (voting) predicted cross-oblast spread better than distance; Kyiv drove the dynamics. Only Mohler is compared against a strong recency baseline; none is directly comparable to our BSS-vs-recent-rate metric.
code_available: Mohler: no official code; widely re-implemented (e.g. open-source ETAS/Hawkes packages such as 'tick', 'hawkeslib', R 'hawkes'/'ETAS', 'PtProcess') [uncertain on authors' code]. Lewis: no public code found. Zammit-Mangion/Cseke: MATLAB code associated with the authors (Zammit-Mangion later released R packages such as FRK/IDE) [uncertain]. Bahid 2024: PLOS ONE data-availability statement; code availability not verified [uncertain]. A literature search (2026-10-17) found no Hawkes study of Ukrainian air-raid alerts [uncertain: absence of evidence from a limited search].
takeaways_for_project: 1) Self-excitation is the right mental model for alert onsets: an onset raises the short-term onset probability in the same and nearby oblasts, decaying over hours. Our D-017 own-state features (minutes_since_last_start, onsets_last_24h/7d) and spatial features (neighbors_active_at_t, national_active_count_at_t) are a discretised, binary-target approximation of a multivariate Hawkes intensity. A cheap, approved-scope extension is an exponentially-decayed onset count with 2-3 fixed half-lives (e.g. 1h, 6h, 24h), computed from starts <= t - stays within 'features from data <= t' but adding features may need human approval per CLAUDE.md. 2) Lewis 2012 warning: without a time-varying background, self-excitation absorbs trend. Our rolling 14-day recent-rate baseline (D-021) is exactly the time-varying background; the model must beat it, not a constant climatology, to claim any excitation signal. 3) Bahid 2024: cross-unit excitation need not follow geography; Kyiv dominated. For alerts, wave-level national coupling (missile/drone waves cross many oblasts) is likely stronger than neighbour adjacency - keep national_active_count_at_t and report per group (Kyiv City / frontline / rear). 4) Dedup first (CLAUDE.md data rule: 113,845 duplicates) and union admin levels per oblast before any excitation statistic; duplicated or raion-split rows masquerade as self-excitation and inflate any branching ratio. 5) Point processes have no duration; alerts do. Our at-risk mask (exclude rows already under alert) and D-020 24h causal cap are necessary additions that the Hawkes literature does not supply. 6) The recording gap must be treated as unobserved (D-013): in Hawkes terms, the likelihood/compensator should skip the gap, and decayed counts spanning it should be NaN/flagged. 7) Regime shifts (Sep-2026 yellow/red) change parameters (Bahid: excitation intensified with the regime); the D-015 calibration-in-the-large check on API data is the right test, and a failed transfer implies refit, consistent with the conditional conclusion rule. 8) Do not add a full Hawkes model as a new model family without explicit approval; at most mention it as future work or as a feature-engineering justification in the README.
best_practices: Adopt: causal-by-construction intensity features (only past onsets); time-varying background (rolling rate) as the null against which excitation is judged; separate in-sample explanation from out-of-sample forecast skill (Zammit-Mangion's one-shot held-out year is the model); prospective day-ahead re-fitting as in Mohler maps to the optional D-014 weekly refit row; report a branching-ratio-like descriptive (share of onsets within X hours of a previous onset) as an EDA fact, not a model claim; residual checks (time-rescaling) as a calibration analogue. Avoid: judging models by in-sample likelihood/AIC only (Lewis, Bahid); contemporaneous exogenous covariates (Bahid's force/injury counts) as predictors; constant background (overstates self-excitation); fitting background KDEs/parameters on the whole period then reporting forecast skill; ignoring tied/duplicate timestamps; treating data gaps as zero events; claiming causal 'contagion' from a fitted kernel - excitation is a statistical clustering summary and common shocks (attack waves) produce the same signature.
